title: Nonlinear Functions, Part 2: Medium and Hard Problems

beats.say: In part one, we evaluated a quadratic and found its vertex, and we saw the factors for exponential growth and decay.
In this video, we work with a doubling model, and then build and use a decay model from a real situation.
Medium example. A culture starts with two hundred bacteria, and the number doubles every three hours. The function is B of t equals two hundred times two to the t over three. Find B of nine.
The exponent is t over three, because the culture doubles every three hours. Replace t with nine.
Nine divided by three is three. This means that nine hours is exactly three doubling periods.
Two cubed is eight. So the culture is multiplied by eight over nine hours.
Two hundred times eight is sixteen hundred. So there are sixteen hundred bacteria after nine hours.

Hard example. A machine is bought for forty-five thousand dollars, and loses twenty percent of its value each year. Write a function for its value after t years, and find the first whole number of years after which the value is below twenty thousand dollars.
Losing twenty percent each year means keeping eighty percent. So the factor is zero point eight, not zero point two. The starting value is forty-five thousand.
Now compute the value year by year. In year one, we multiply forty-five thousand by zero point eight, and get thirty-six thousand dollars.
In year two, we multiply thirty-six thousand by zero point eight, and get twenty-eight thousand eight hundred dollars.
In year three, the value is twenty-three thousand forty dollars. That is still above twenty thousand, so three years is not enough.
In year four, the value is eighteen thousand four hundred thirty-two dollars, which is below twenty thousand.
So the value first drops below twenty thousand dollars after four years. Remember that the question asks for a whole number of years, and year three was still too high.

One more skill. In vertex form, f of x equals a times x minus h, squared, plus k, the vertex is h comma k. For two times x plus three, squared, minus seven, h is negative three, and k is negative seven.
To recap. In a doubling model, the exponent is t divided by the doubling time, not t times it.
beats.item: Doubling: the exponent is t over d

beats.say: A twenty percent decrease means a factor of zero point eight. Compute year by year, and answer in whole years.
In vertex form, the sign inside the parentheses is reversed. In the next video, we look at common traps and the fast way with Desmos.
